summary: Adds field membership attributes, typically Weight and optionally distance, by testing points against 3D shapes such as spheres, boxes, tubes, capsules, planes, parabola fields, and line projections. Multiple fields can be driven by a specification POP whose attributes match parameter tokens.

key_params.name: fieldattrscope
key_params.note: Output attribute scope for the field weight

key_params.name: specpop
key_params.note: Optional POP where each point defines one field specification

key_params.name: mode
key_params.note: Field shape such as sphere, box, torus, tube, capsule, plane, parabola, or line projection

key_concepts: Field POP evaluates points, vertices, or primitives against analytic 3D fields and writes field membership as attributes such as Weight or signed distance.
Supported field modes include sphere/ellipsoid, box, torus, tube variants, capsule, axis planes, parabola, and line projection.
Specification POP lets one point define one field by supplying attributes whose names match Field POP parameter tokens; P is a special shortcut for tx, ty, and tz.
Transition Range, Transition Align, and Transition Type shape the falloff from inside to outside, while range, invert, and absolute-value controls reshape the output values.
Multiple fields can be blended into one Weight attribute or emitted as raw per-field array attributes for downstream logic.
The Output page can write weight, signed distance, per-field weights/distances, or combine the field result into another attribute such as PartForce.
common_gotchas: Specification POP attributes must use parameter token names; P is special and maps to tx, ty, and tz.
Weight can be blended across multiple fields and capped at 1 unless raw per-field outputs are requested.
Field POP is often a mask source; multiply Weight into attributes such as PartForce rather than deleting data too early.
